title: CERT-In warns of flaws in Asus Control Center and Armoury Crate; Asus has shipped fixes
date_note: digit.in's page gives only 'Updated on 27-Nov-2026'; BleepingComputer, dated 19 November, reports the Asus fixes released that day.
summary: digit.in reports that India's CERT-In warned of flaws in Asus Control Center Express, Datacenter and Enterprise and in Armoury Crate that could give attackers administrator access. BleepingComputer, citing Asus, says Control Center Express flaws are fixed in v1.7.29, including CVE-2026-114202, a hard-coded key flaw that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker forge an authentication token. Neither page reports exploitation.
plain: Indian authorities warn that some Asus management software has flaws that could let attackers take admin control. Asus has released updates.
exec: A CERT-In warning covers Asus management tools, including a flaw BleepingComputer says allows unauthenticated remote admin access.
action: CERT-In advises checking whether affected versions are in use and installing the latest security updates; Asus says to install Control Center Express v1.7.29.
geo_basis: country: CERT-In, India's national CERT, issued the warning

sources.name: BleepingComputer: Asus warns of critical hard-coded key flaw in Control Center Express
digit.in: Using Asus devices? Hackers can bypass security and take control of your system, govt warns

validation.note: BleepingComputer (citing Asus) and digit.in (citing CERT-In) independently report the flaws in Control Center and Armoury Crate; Asus's and CERT-In's own pages were not read.
